definition: Expansive means spread out over a wide area or ranging across a wide scope — broad, open, and still opening outward.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word expansive. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know expansive should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: From the fire tower the view is expansive — four counties, two rivers, and on clear mornings the faint smudge of the city.
Broad is weaker than expansive: broad states a generous width and stops there, while expansive adds openness — the sense that the spread keeps going past where you expected it to end.
Boundless is stronger than expansive: an expansive lawn still ends at a fence line somewhere, but boundless claims no limit exists at all.

covering a great span in one motion — a sweeping view, a sweeping claim — and, applied to statements, it often hints the reach went too far to be careful. Expansive is roomy without the warning label.

When Prospect City rebuilt its waterfront, the designers argued for weeks about one word in the brief: the park had to feel expansive.
Big was easy — the city owned two hundred acres.
The trick was making two hundred acres feel like more, not less.
A visitor never sees the whole lawn at once; each bend opens a meadow that wasn't visible a moment before.
Fences came down, sight lines run out to the water, and the far shore reads as part of the park even though it isn't.
On opening day a reviewer wrote that the grounds seem to keep unfolding as you walk — which was, the lead designer said, the whole assignment.
